movesLifeStageScale.citation: Scales the American Community Survey 2024 rate of leaving the county for a person's age band and state (data/research/migration/mover-rates-acs-2024.json) into their monthly pull to leave, so that a town's departures over a year, after each person's own ties hold some back, land on that rate. Calibrated in src/core2/moves.test.ts.

movesOwnerHold.citation: How much owning the home holds a household in place: in the year to March 2023, 1.85% of people in owner-occupied homes moved to a different county against 6.23% of people in rented homes (Census, CPS ASEC 2023, Table 1 'General Mobility in the Past Year, by Tenure', mig_01_2023_1yr.xlsx, rows 66-67, column I); ln(6.23/1.85) = 1.21.

movesChildrenHold.citation: How much school-age children at home hold a household in place. Families with school-age children move less than those without (Census, Current Population Survey ASEC 2023 mobility tables by family type); the size is a starting value.

movesKinHold.citation: How much each close relative living in town holds a person there, up to movesKinHoldCap relatives. People with kin nearby are less likely to leave (Spring, Ackert, Crowder and South 2017, Demography 54(4):1277-1304).

movesKinHoldCap.citation: How many relatives in town count toward holding a person there.

movesJobHold.citation: How much a job holds a person in place: 3.66% of employed civilians moved to a different county in the year to March 2023 against 5.93% of the unemployed (Census, CPS ASEC 2023, Table 2 'General Mobility by Labor Force Status', mig_02_2023_1yr.xlsx, rows 9 and 11, column I); ln(5.93/3.66) = 0.48. The unemployed sample is small (6.2 million people).

movesJobLostPull.citation: The push a lost job adds toward leaving town. 'To look for work or lost job' is 1.5% of movers' reasons (Census CPS ASEC 2023, Table 13), and displaced workers move across county lines more than others, but most stay.

movesKinMovedPull.citation: The push a parent, child or sibling moving away adds toward following them. 'Other family reason' is 7.9% of movers' reasons (Census CPS ASEC 2023, Table 13).

movesStayPull.citation: What staying weighs against the built-up pull to leave in the monthly choice; the pull is measured on this scale.

movesMinimumAge.citation: The youngest age band in the American Community Survey 2024 departure rates this engine reads (18 and 19); younger people move with their household.

movesRiskWeight.citation: How much a person's trait lean toward moving away over staying put (every trait through the shared trait table, about -1 to 1; OPUS-TRAITS, Oct 12, 2026) loosens what holds them in town (a lean toward staying tightens it). Personality predicts moving within and between US states (Jokela 2009, Journal of Research in Personality 43(1):79-83); the size is a starting value.
